title: Forward Chaining over Horn Clauses
description: Repeatedly scan a list of Horn rules and add derived conclusions to the facts set until a pass adds nothing new.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Initialize `facts = {"A", "B"}` and represent each Horn clause in `rules` as a `(premises_set, conclusion)` pair.

Use a `while changed:` loop that resets `changed = False` and tests every rule with `premises <= facts and conclusion not in facts`. Add any new `conclusion` to `facts` and set `changed = True`. Print the sorted `facts` when the loop terminates.
Look at line 10: `premises <= facts` uses Python set inclusion to check whether every premise of the rule is already in `facts`. `conclusion not in facts` ensures each rule fires at most once.

steps.question: Why does the `while changed:` loop run a second pass after the first `for` loop finishes?
steps.answer: The first pass adds `'C'`, `'D'`, and `'E'` and sets `changed = True`. The second pass checks all three rules again and finds no new conclusions to add. It leaves `changed = False` and stops at the fixpoint.

steps.description: When `premises <= facts` holds for `({"A", "B"}, "C")`, line 12 adds `"C"` to `facts` so later rules can use it.
Once a full pass over `rules` leaves `changed == False`, line 14 prints `Derived knowledge base: ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']`.
